waterMl.notes: No change from FitPlate general water target; hypothyroidism alone does not change water needs and no thyroid-specific fluid number was found. Never pushed higher: severe untreated hypothyroidism can impair water excretion and cause low sodium (myxedema coma, an emergency). Take the thyroid tablet with plain water. Drink more in heat, exercise or fever per general rules. With heart, kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or diuretics, show only the general range. Follow your doctor's advice.

warnings: General information, not medical advice. FitPlate does not diagnose hypothyroidism; a doctor's examination and blood tests are needed.
The app never suggests starting, stopping or changing levothyroxine or any thyroid medicine, dose, brand or schedule. Follow your doctor.

Do not take iodine, kelp or seaweed supplements, or 'thyroid support' pills, without a doctor; the ATA advises against iodine or kelp supplements above 500 µg/day, and people with Hashimoto's are susceptible to harm from excess iodine.
Selenium supplements: evidence is limited; upper limit 400 µg/day from all sources (NIH); do not self-start.
High-dose biotin can distort thyroid blood tests; tell your doctor and lab.
Calcium and iron tablets are commonly kept about 4 hours from levothyroxine; coffee, soy and high-fibre foods can lower absorption. Follow the schedule your doctor gives.
Thyroid treatment does not reliably cause weight loss (ATA).
Use iodised salt within the 5 g/day limit; do not cut out salt entirely or swap to non-iodised salt without advice.
Emergency: extreme drowsiness, confusion, very low body temperature, very slow breathing or fainting with known hypothyroidism. Seek emergency care now (112).
With heart, kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or diuretics, follow your doctor's advice on fluids.
requires_doctor_input is true because thyroid disease needs a doctor-set diagnosis, monitoring and medicine dose, and pregnancy changes thyroid and iodine needs.
